title: Scaffolding Projectile Motion from Flat Ground to Inclined Obstacles
physical_system: Point particle under constant downward gravity g

rungs.physical_delta: Baseline symmetric ground-to-ground projectile motion over horizontal terrain
rungs.mathematical_complexity: Single-formula evaluation of range, flight time, and apex height
rungs.transfer_requirement: Resolving initial velocity into orthogonal horizontal and vertical components

rungs.physical_delta: Asymmetric trajectory from an elevated platform of height h above target level
rungs.mathematical_complexity: Solving quadratic kinematic equation in time for asymmetric boundary conditions
rungs.transfer_requirement: Enforcing sign convention for downward displacement y = -h

rungs.physical_delta: Landing target situated on an inclined boundary y = x tan(beta)
rungs.mathematical_complexity: Simultaneous solution of parabolic trajectory and linear boundary constraint
rungs.transfer_requirement: Parametric intersection of ballistic trajectory with geometric slope

rungs.physical_delta: Full inclined coordinate transformation with orthogonal components of gravity along and normal to incline
rungs.mathematical_complexity: 2D accelerated motion with non-zero acceleration components on both axes
rungs.transfer_requirement: Tilted reference frame analysis and optimal launch angle derivation theta = pi/4 + beta/2

pedagogical_objective: Scaffold 2D projectile mechanics from elementary symmetric ground launch through asymmetric height offsets to inclined plane projection with tilted reference frames.
